newsitem.title: CANADA: Burmese deny Canadian envoy access to Suu Kyi.
newsitem.headline: Burmese deny Canadian envoy access to Suu Kyi.

text.p: The Burmese government has blocked Canada's ambassador to Rangoon from visiting Aung San Suu Kyi, prompting Canadian worries that the government may be trying to tighten access to the Burmese democracy leader.

Ambassador Manfred von Nostitz tried to visit Suu Kyi on Wednesday evening, but Burmese security officials met him and prevented him from entering her compound, Canadian foreign affairs spokeswoman Diane Simsovik said on Friday.
"It's not acceptable that he was denied access to Miss Suu Kyi, and the ambassador raised the issue with Burmese minister of foreign affairs the next day," she said.
He was told he would have to make requests to the Burmese Foreign Ministry if he wanted to visit her.

"Canada is very concerned that these new procedures might make it far more difficult to have meetings with Aung San Suu Kyi and with the leadership of the National League for Democracy," Simsovik said.

She added that the ambassador left Burma on a previously planned flight on Thursday but would continue to seek meetings with Suu Kyi, who won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize for her non-violent efforts toward democracy.
